newsitem.title: UK: Worldwide Advertising & Media Digest - May 1.
newsitem.headline: Worldwide Advertising & Media Digest - May 1.

text.p: ....REUTERS WORLDWIDE ADVERTISING & MEDIA DIGEST.....
Reuters news from around the world on Advertising, Marketing, Media, the Internet, Brand-name Products and Consumer Trends
ADVERTISING & MARKETING:

WASHINGTON - The U.S. tobacco industry would accept a ban on all cigarette vending machines, halt all outdoor advertising and pay hundreds of millions a year for anti-smoking campaigns as part of a package of concessions in exchange for immunity, the Washington Post reports.

DARMSTADT, Germany - German cosmetics group Wella AG and Italian luxury goods company Gucci N.V. have agreed to expand their cooperation on Gucci perfume promotion, Wella says. Wella, the licencee for Gucci perfumes, says it would take charge of international marketing, production and distribution. Gucci will retain control of all creative and image aspects including product design, advertising and public relations activities.

NEW YORK - Interpublic Group of Cos Inc is expected to announce it has taken a minority stake in Nicholson New York, a firm which helps companies determine what to do on the Web, the Wall Street Journal says. Terms would not be disclosed, the newspaper says.
MEDIA & THE INTERNET:

NEW YORK - Time Warner Inc plans to unplug its interactive television network in Orlando, Florida by year-end, the Wall Street Journal reports in its electronic edition. The newspaper says the company is "all but abandoning" plans to employ its cable systems for use in a nationwide shopping and entertainment interactive service. The network in Florida let subscribers order movies and pizza and play interactive games.

MILAN - Italian multi-media group Mediaset sees 1997 as a year of strong growth with advertising revenue already up 10 percent in the first three months of the year, chairman Fedele Confalonieri says. The television and advertising group, part of Silvio Berlusconi's Fininvest SpA empire, posted 1996 pre-tax profit of 835.4 billion lire ($488.3 million) against 578.1 billion.

PARIS - A pricing row is delaying French cable television firms from offering Internet access on their networks, the companies involved say. Telecommunications regulator ART (Autorite de Regulation des Telecommunications) is due to rule in July on complaints from Lyonnaise Cable, part of Lyonnaise des Eaux, and Compagnie Generale de Videocommunication (CGV), part of Generale des Eaux, that the price asked by France Telecom for a high-speed gateway to cyberspace was too high.

DENVER - Armed with figures showing better operating cash flow, a key barometer in the cable TV industry, Tele-Communications Inc Chief Executive John Malone says the company's recent bad times are behind it. "Our core cable business is now restored to its vitality, has clear operating plans in place ... and a strong financial base by which to do it," Malone tells reporters.
NEW DELHI - The Indian cabinet has approved a proposed law to throw open broadcasting to private firms, but the law would limit foreign partners to minority shareholdings, a senior official says.

PARIS - French online information service company Infonie, faced with slower than expected growth in subscriber numbers, is planning a capital increase and a link-up with another company, a spokeswoman says.

HAARLEM, Netherlands - Dutch publisher VNU says it has agreed to take a 50-percent stake in RCV Entertainment, an independent film, video and television distribution company based in Hilversum, Netherlands. RCV is the largest independent distributor in the Benelux countries, with a catalogue of around 1,000 American feature films.
BRAND-NAME PRODUCTS & MARKETS:

SAN FRANCISCO - Electronic Arts Inc's chief executive, Larry Probst, says he expects the worldwide market for video game software to rise to $11 billion by 1999. "We see the software business growing 15 to 20 percent overall this year," Probst tells a conference in San Francisco.

EINDHOVEN, Netherlands - Philips Electronics NV says it has introduced its first digital video disc (DVD) player in the U.S. and is planning a DVD rental programme with PolyGram Video. Philips says its Magnavox 400AT player will be available through U.S. retailers at a suggested retal price of $549.

NEW YORK - Tyson Foods Inc enters into agreement with the Kuok Group's Kerry Holdings Ltd to study feasability of building 10 poultry production plants in the People's Republic of China. Tyson said it expects construction to begin in the first half of 1998.

TOKYO - A boost in Japan's sales tax on April 1 sharply cut into vehicle sales during the month, resulting in the first sales drop in eight months, an industry body says. Vehicle sales fell 12.7 percent in April from a year earlier to 326,975 units, the Japan Automobile Dealers' Association says.
CONSUMER TRENDS:

WASHINGTON - Watch out New York. Move over Los Angeles. Washington is trying to shed its dowdy image and become the hair styling capital of the United States. That is the aim of Dennis Roche, hair stylist and owner of Roche Salon. "Washington is notoriously looked down upon in the fashion industry ... you don't have the fashion celebrities or the entertainment celebrities," says Roche.

PERTH, Australia - Sleeping with the enemy, wok oil and weight loss are all part of an Australian drive to put more wool back into the wardrobes of the world's fashion buyers. Faced with changing fashion, reluctance among consumers to splash out on a new suit and a public perception that wool is hot and heavy, the wool industry is looking to lighten up. Fashion houses are being encouraged to weave lycra and polyesters into their wool clothes, reducing the weight of some garments and providing "extra bounce".

BELGRADE - Yugoslavia registered 458,629 tourists in the first quarter of 1997, down 17.3 percent from the same period last year, the Federal Statistics Office reports. Of the total, Yugoslavs numbered 404,046, or 18.4 less than in January-March 1996. The number of foreign tourists dropped 14.1 percent from a year earlier. Most foreign visitors came from Italy, Germany, Bulgaria, Greece and Austria.
